This page summarizes the organization and assessment of the course. The [syllabus](../../syllabus.qmd) is the reference document; if anything here differs from it, the syllabus applies.

## Lectures and laboratories

The course has 40 sessions: 18 lectures, 12 computer laboratory sessions, 5 sessions for the group project and 5 for assessment. Lectures and labs alternate. A lecture introduces a model and its analysis; the next lab implements, simulates and visualizes it in Python. Simulations built in a lab are reused in later lectures.

The course is organized in seven parts:

- Part I, low-dimensional deterministic dynamics (this module).
- Part II, synchronization and collective behaviour.
- Part III, modelling with randomness.
- Part IV, space and pattern formation.
- Part V, complex networks.
- Part VI, explorables and discrete models.
- Part VII, assessment and group project.

## Assessment

| Item | Weight | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Assignments | 20% | Two hand-in assignments, 10% each: the Kuramoto model and pattern formation |
| Explorables presentation | 10% | Presentation in pairs of a model from the Complexity Explorables collection |
| Exam | 25% | Individual, multiple choice, after the course material has been covered |
| Group project | 45% | Groups of three: written report, poster, short video and oral defence |

You need at least 3.5 in the individual exam to pass the course.

The two graded assignments are:

- [Kuramoto assignment](../collective-behaviour/assignment-kuramoto.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary}
- [Pattern formation assignment](../pattern-formation/assignment-patterns.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary}

Pages called "practice" in this module are ungraded. Use them to prepare for the assignments and the project.

## Use of generative AI

You may use generative AI tools as a learning aid and as a coding aid, and you should acknowledge that use. You may not use them to solve homework assignments or during the exam. The syllabus gives the full policy and a suggested acknowledgement format.

## What you need

- Python with the packages in `requirements.txt` of the [course repository](https://github.com/daniprec/BAM-Applied-Math-Lab). See [Reproducible Code](reproducibility.qmd).
- The compulsory textbook, @strogatz2024nonlinear. Each session page lists its readings in a callout at the top.
